Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
LSJ wrote:
>
> Curevei wrote:
> > Pander could use some clan cards.
>
> A minority opinion, I think.

I agree with him. That'd be two to one. :-}

> Pander do not lend themselves to mono-clan deckbuilding except in weenie
> decks. Weenie decks need no boosts currently.

I don't think that's a valid observation. When you build a weenie deck,
you generally don't conform to clan limitations of any kind at all, unless
you need what Gomi calls a "clan toy" or two. But to the extent you
attempt to conform your weenie deck to the need for such a thing, it
constrains what weenies you can use. For instance, if I want to put enough
Malkavians into my weeny deck featuring the cheapest minions that have
inferior obfuscate to support Muddled Vampire Hunters, I have to start going
up it bit in capsize.

I can see the reluctance to print anything really powerful or very many
things, but right now it's hard to find any reason to play Pander at all.
Ghouled Street Thug is overcosted and has little synergy with most Pander
anyway. And while current Legacy of Pander is possibly worth using IF
you're building a LoP deck for other reasons, it's really not a good
enough reason to build one by itself. (And it's worthless to build a
partial Pander deck to get, unlike the Muddled Vampire Hunter example
above with Malkavian weenies - since the fewer Pander you put in, the
fewer potential votes you'll get from it.)

PAID POLITICAL ANNOUNCEMENT:
Pander could really use at least another good clan card, if not a few,
to make things interesting.

THIS HAS BEEN A PAID POLITICAL ANNOUNCEMENT!

Fred

Fine. But doubling up has its own problems as well. I didn't say they
were very bad problems, necessarily. In this case I'd say they're pretty
slight whichever way you go. I was just demonstrating the point that
confining your weenies to a single clan weakens the crypt. In the case
of Pander (or Caitiff, were that a clan), the problem is much worse
because their disciplines aren't almost entirely confined to three choices.

> >I can see the reluctance to print anything really powerful or very many
> >things, but right now it's hard to find any reason to play Pander at all.
>
> There are, of course, many other non-weenie clans for which it is easy
> to find reasons to play. Perhaps the current designers intend to move
> the game away from weenies.

Maybe. But given that much more powerful weeny decks already exist, I'm
just suggesting that it wouldn't hurt anything to let people have some
actual fun with a Pander clan deck. I don't think it's much problem to
do that in a way that won't make the truly powerful weeny decks any
worse. So I suppose that would involve making sure you don't give them
something that can be easily integrated into a deck with three or four
Pander and eight or nine other vampires that are organized around a
discipline instead of the Pander clan.

Fred

your point; however, those of us who know the truth are not fooled.

>> See the X/anti-X pattern?
>
>Hardly. I don't see where any "anti-weeny" decks even enter the
>discussion. They're not necessary.

Pay attention, Freddie. You'll see the X/anti-X if you look.

>So none of this has anything to do with decks Derek would like to play
>were it not for all those stinkin' weenies running around? I don't know
>what issues you have with this but it would be inane to think that poor
>l'il Panders can't a lousy break because Derek Rey is scared to death of
>disciplineless weenies running around with Computer Hacks and Dodges.

That is correct, Fred, none of it has ANYTHING to do with any decks that
I personally would like to play; I play them anyway, whether or not I
think I'll see the Weenie Computer Hack Dodge Horde. I do not argue
from personal bias, unlike you. I believe that anything which reduces
the variety of viable decks is a Bad Thing, whether or not I want to
play those decks. You, on the other hand, evince a clear clan
preference, and have in the past evinced both an anti-combat bias
(because weenies die to combat), and a pro-weenie preference. Assuming
that you can make a fair judgement on this would be a laugher; you are
far more likely to just be munchkinning out and hoping to sneak one by.

Giving Pander a clan card improves weenie decks, because the Pander are
a weenie clan. Improving weenie decks reduces the variety of decks
which are viable at a tournament table.

Therefore, while giving Pander a clan card would improve the variety of
viable decks in a small fashion (for Pander), it would reduce that
variety by far more than it would improve it, leading to a net loss.

Action

> negligible) to hang on and do something else.

I don't expect to convince you, since your arguments seemed based mainly
upon your experience rather than any kind of first principles, but I do
consider the "One Cap Hack" deck to be a serious threat, and chalk up its
lack of popularity more to social factors than competitive ones.

Sure weenie pre/dom/pot/for/whatever gets access to discipline tricks the
one cap deck doesn't have, but they are... what? Two to three times as
big, ergo two to three times as slow. The strength of the 1CH lies in
it's "one-ness". Where most people fail with that deck is not paying
enough attention to maintaining the steady flow of ablative
minions. *That's* why it gets one VP and stalls, if it actually stalls.

I see this deck played, Fred. I see it win. And we don't suck, and for a
while, *not* building your deck to deal with weenies around here was
suicide. I was prepared for it, everybody knew the deal, and it still
won. Not every time, but often enough. Best as I can recall, though,
it's prey was just about always screwed. I'll side with Derek, so far as
what the deck is capable of doing.

Oh heck, I just remembered... here's an anecdote for you: brought a noob
with us to the SE Qualfier in Atlanta. Put the 1CH in his hands. He got
his prey *every game*, and a few more besides. No, he didn't win. But he
also barely knew the game, and that's how he did. What's your anecdote?

And I will never, ever, everevereverever buy your argument that "If it
makes people gang up on it and they can sometimes stop it that way, then
it isn't broken". But we've had this argument before; nothing new to
say.
